reason: Batch of independently reviewed PRs, each green on its own: #1036: /api/v1/health derived api_ready and status from SQL only (a promoted API row with a live lease), so a frozen or hung API worker was reported ready indefinitely and a killed one until the next 5 s reconciliation while every API call failed. Health now asks the promoted worker for its identity over the signed worker RPC (1 s timeout, 1 s cache) and reports api_state ready/not_responding/unavailable, with api_ready and status following it; static-asset routing keeps the SQL-only check (api_promoted). The UI keeps its memory-budget recovery screen for held admission only (api_state unavailable). The deployer's wait_ready() and wait_supervisor_host_ready() now also require one authenticated API read. The selection covers supervisor health and recovery (real promoted API worker frozen/killed), management, host knowledge bootstrap health, deployer readiness waits, the UI health mapping and both recovery-screen suites. #1031: RuntimeProcessHost._adopt_origin replaced the worker socket directory only when the boot changed or the directory was missing; a recorded path that existed but was not a private owner-only directory of this user (another local user recreating a vanished /tmp name, loosened permissions, a symlink) made start() raise a bare ValueError, so systemd restart-looped Core. On the same origin it is now replaced like a missing directory (fresh mkdtemp root, atomically replaced marker, reason socket_root_untrusted) without reusing, following, repairing or deleting the recorded path and without presuming any worker dead; with a same-boot PID-namespace change it is refused with the existing clear conflict and the marker untouched. The selection covers host start, rediscovery, retirement and reconciliation with real detached workers, including 8 new regressions (foreign-owned, shared-mode and symlinked directories; refusal in another namespace). #1035: After a host reboot every memory-runner job whose launch owner was a process of the old boot stayed charged forever, and a held job also blocked every coordinated shutdown (runtime-stop): MemoryReconciler._reconcile and MemoryBudgetService.release_prelaunch(owner_dead=True) both required the owner's recorded process origin to equal the current one. A parseable earlier kernel boot now proves the owner ended with its kernel on this host (process_identity.launch_owner_ended, shared by both checks); because a host sharing the database would look the same, the supervisor's reconciler also requires RuntimeProcessHost.boot_ended (no unretired runtime born on that boot still renews a lease), and project-worker reconcilers leave such jobs to it. Only never-launched reservations are released on that proof; starting and launched jobs keep the uncertain / verified-removal paths. The selection covers the reconciler, prelaunch release and its guards, host memory recovery, rediscovery/lease helpers and origin parsing, including 14 new regressions. #1027: The kernel's web search install/test/engines routes ran the now-async SearchRuntime.record through asyncio.to_thread, so the coroutine was never awaited and the digest, last test and engines were never saved. They now await it. Selected: the Butler admin settings suite, whose web search journey test fails on main, and the web search suite. #1018: Host pressure's waiting reason embedded the live reading (e.g. 'CPU use (99% >= 80%)'). Queued chat turns, missions and harness turns save that text, so each change in the reading rewrote every waiting record (a real Core turn reached ~50 revisions in 17 minutes; up to one write and one queued stream frame per second) and widened stale-revision windows for harness and mission Stop. The reason now names only the metric and threshold. Selected: host load sampling/admission (with the new regression test), host pressure settings and admission, shared runtime capacity waits, Butler host-load reads, and the host-load-admission browser journey that shows the queued notice. #1042: The legacy nebula-chat Butler chat (chat_cli.stream) and the shared sync request() helper treated a supervisor Core's 202 saved-request receipt as the end of the stream or as the result, so a first message to a cold project printed 'Connection ended before completion' while Core ran it and sync mutations returned the receipt. Same bug #1034 fixed for the TUI. The change reuses #1034's accepted_receipt() to follow runtime/requests/{id}/response (stream and sync) for up to two minutes without resending. Selected: the new legacy receipt regression tests (they fail on pristine main with the reported error), the shared transport contracts, and the legacy chat CLI suite. #1011: Test-only repair of two #939 leftovers in test_butler_resources.py that fail on main: one passed an async function as ChatService's synchronous provider_usage_observer (never awaited), the other read the async store.get inside a synchronous storage listener lambda (raised and was swallowed). The product wires only the synchronous OpenRouterCreditObserver.schedule and storage awaits listeners via call_async, so product behaviour is unchanged; the tests now exercise those contracts again. The whole file is selected. #1054: Several Core routes answer 202 as their final response (missions, report renders, run retry, executions, draft notes, continue-as-mission, browser lease commands). Since 6607313 the GUI followed every 202 as a receipt, so a replayed final 202 looked pending: the GUI polled for 120 s and showed "Your request is saved", or showed it at once against a direct Core. Core now marks every receipt-following answer with X-Nebula-Request-State (complete / pending / needs-reconciliation) through one replay-header helper used by the API worker and Host Settings; the GUI, terminal client and Settings bridge stop on anything but pending, and without the marker treat only Core's receipt, status and chat-acceptance envelopes as pending. Selection: the API worker suite (new marker tests for receipt, status, final 202 replay on GET and POST retry, spoofed saved marker, 409, chat acceptance and stream hand-off, plus the existing replay and viewer tests), Host Settings replay, pending, uncertain and paired-receipt tests, the two Settings bridge tests that exercise the complete (not pending) path, the terminal transport suite (new marker and chat-acceptance cases) and the two terminal shell tests that follow saved receipts. Frontend: client.test.ts (its three cases red on main since 6607313 now pass), client.durableRequests.test.ts (new final-202, older/direct Core and chat-acceptance cases), durableRequests.test.ts and executionDraftTransport.test.ts (draft-note 202s). #1057: #1022 turned a confirmed-clean spawn abort into StartAborted, which hid the original reason ('worker startup exited; inspect its private diagnostic log') behind a generic message and changed the timed-out start from TimeoutError, so two process-level tests in test_runtime_processes.py fail on main. StartAborted now keeps the operator-facing reason of a CoordinationConflict or RuntimeIpcError (other errors by type only), and the timeout test expects StartAborted caused by TimeoutError. Selected: the process-level spawn tests and automatic recovery, which consumes StartAborted.

On this shared host at load average 35-45, spawn-heavy cases there (test_actual_supervisor_process_exit_leaves_worker_reachable, test_real_api_promotion_keeps_old_worker_until_replacement_is_ready) miss their 15-20 s startup deadlines intermittently on both pristine main (4 failures in one run) and this branch (1 failure in the same run); no selected test fails only with this change. The real-Core release of a previous-boot reservation and the unblocked runtime-stop are recorded in the PR. #1027: Supervisor Cores serve these routes from the host (runtime_integration_effects.py), which already awaits record, so no real-Core journey differs; no UI, native or Playwright cases. #1018: test_butler_host_load.py::test_host_load_is_discoverable_read_only_and_rereads_core and test_host_cpu_budget.py (11 cases) fail identically on pristine origin/main and with this patch, so they are excluded. Real-Core evidence (scratch Postgres Core, forced CPU threshold: a queued turn's revision 1 -> 33 in 40 s on main vs 2 -> 2 with this patch) is recorded in the PR, not executed by CI. #1042: No full suites. No frontend, native or Playwright changes: only the separate Python terminal client and docs/CLI.md changed. tests/v3/test_chat_cli_core.py is not selected: its headless Core case fails identically on pristine origin/main locally (the headless Core process exits during startup in this environment). Supervisor 202 receipts do not occur on the create_app fixture Core; MockTransport regression tests cover them. No live provider calls or Core deployment. #1011: No product code changed, so no other Python suites, UI, native or Playwright cases are selected, and no real-Core check applies. #1054: Not selected: test_runtime_host_settings.py's process-level tests (test_saved_session_credential_serves_first_chat_in_an_actual_retained_kernel, test_session_secret_rpc_requires_the_exact_lease_and_current_provider_reference), which also fail locally on origin/main, and the rest of that file and the bridge file, which do not reach the changed replay paths. No native code changed. PostgreSQL parametrizations are collected but skip in CI because these files are not in the workflow's PostgreSQL list; they passed locally on PostgreSQL 16. The legacy nebula-chat client (#1042, unmerged) uses the same accepted_receipt and gains the marker when it lands. No live or staging Core mutation, database backup, or deployment. #1057: test_runtime_processes.py spawns real workers; locally it was run with a per-worktree Python 3.12 venv whose nebula resolves to this worktree. Under this host's load (load ~32) two cases timed out once and passed on rerun. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed.
